New airplanes. Future first solos. ✈️

Clover Park Technical College in Puyallup, Washington, welcomed six new Cessna 172S Skyhawks on October 14, bringing its training fleet to 18 aircraft.

The ribbon cutting took place at the college’s South Hill Campus at Pierce County Airport/Thun Field—a local airport helping the next generation learn to fly.

For a pilot-training program approaching 80 years, it’s a fresh chapter built around a familiar general aviation workhorse. The college also offers aviation maintenance and avionics technician programs, connecting the cockpit with the people who keep airplanes flying.

New trainers mean years of lessons ahead: checklists, pattern work, cross-country planning and that unforgettable first flight without an instructor beside you.

Here’s to the students, instructors and maintainers writing the next chapter at Thun Field. Blue skies! 💙

Source: General Aviation News, October 18, 2026.
